div.h2: In this last section, you’ll digitally sign your federal tax return.
div.p: Instead of physically signing your tax return, you’ll each create a new Self-Select PIN to digitally sign this year’s federal tax return.
If you completed a federal tax return last year, you will need one of these from last year’s federal tax return:

ul.li: Last year’s Adjusted Gross Income (AGI), or
Last year’s 5-digit Self-Select PIN

div.p: Instead of physically signing your tax return, you’ll each create a new Self-Select PIN that will confirm your identity.
If you completed a federal tax return last year, you will need one of these from last year’s federal tax return:

ul.li: Last year’s Adjusted Gross Income (AGI), or
Last year’s 5-digit Self-Select PIN

p.modal-link: Where can I find last year’s Adjusted Gross Income (AGI) or Self-Select PIN?

modal-dialog.modal-heading: Where can I find my Adjusted Gross Income (AGI) or Self-Select PIN from last year?

p.strong: Fastest way to find last year’s AGI

ul.li: The fastest way to get your AGI is by selecting use last year’s AGI to confirm your identity. Direct File can look it up.

p.strong: Other ways to find your AGI

ul.li: Sign in to your IRS online account. Your AGI will be shown in the Return Summary section under Tax Records.
If you have a copy of your federal tax return, the AGI will be listed on line 11 of your Form 1040. Get a copy of your return by logging in to the tax software you used, or contact your tax preparer.

p.strong: Ways to find last year’s Self-Select PIN

ul.li: If you used a tax preparer, check Form 8879 to see if it’s listed there.
If you used tax software, download a copy of your tax return to see if it’s listed there.

modal-content.p: Note: If you didn’t file a federal tax return last year, you don’t need to find this information.

div.h2: In order to file your federal tax return electronically, you’ll need your Self-Select PIN or Adjusted Gross Income (AGI).

fg-alert.heading: You can file your federal taxes only as a paper tax return

p.strong: You can file your federal taxes only as a paper tax return because you’re missing last year’s Adjusted Gross Income (AGI) or Self-Select PIN.

fg-detail.p: Paper returns can take up to 6 weeks to process.
Your AGI or Self-Select PIN from last year’s federal tax return is needed to confirm your identity. If you can’t find either, you won’t be able to file your tax return electronically.
Try following these instructions to retrieve your AGI. Or you may continue to file by paper. If you need assistance, chat with customer support.

div.h2: Enter your Self-Select PIN from last year’s federal tax return.

p.modal-link: Where can I find last year’s Self-Select PIN?

div.h2: Enter your Adjusted Gross Income (AGI) from last year’s federal tax return.
div.p: Direct File looks up your AGI from your IRS account.
Direct File looks up the AGI from the IRS account for .

If you and your spouse filed your federal tax return using the Married Filing Jointly filing status, you probably have the same AGI. If you didn’t file together, you should look up your AGI to make sure you enter the right number.
